claim: JPMorgan analysts (Sept 2022 note) forecast Apple would move 5% of global iPhone 14 production to India by late 2022 and scale India's share to 25% of all iPhones by 2025 -- a roughly 2.5-year lead time to quintuple share from a 5% base.
stance_target: manufacturing diversification is physically slow, load-bearing capex-to-output lead-time figure for India iPhone assembly
scope_conditions: iPhone (all models) production share, India only; forecast made in Sept 2022 targeting late 2022 and 2025
quoted_support: Apple will move 5% of global iPhone 14 production to India by late 2022, and expand its manufacturing capacity in the country to produce 25% of all iPhones by 2025.

claim: Once an EMS vendor already has established production capability, catching up a brand-new iPhone model's India production to the China start date required only two to three months in 2022 -- a much shorter lag than the multi-year timelines needed to build NEW capacity or share from scratch.
stance_target: distinguishes ramp-up-on-existing-base speed from new-capacity-build speed
scope_conditions: iPhone 14/14 Plus non-Pro models only, India, 4Q22, existing EMS vendor relationship (not a new factory)
quoted_support: Apple has requested that EMS vendors manufacture iPhone 14/14 Plus models in India in 4Q22, within two to three months of the start of production in Mainland China. The much shorter interval implies the increasing importance of India production.

claim: Foxconn's Indian iPhone assembly operation had over 20,000 operators in 2022 versus 350,000 in China -- a roughly 17x labor-scale gap illustrating the distance from parity even after India's ramp had begun.
stance_target: manufacturing diversification is physically slow at scale, despite headline share-shift narratives
quoted_support: Foxconn currently has over 20,000 operators in its iPhone assembly business in India, compared to 350,000 of those in China, the analysts estimated.
